About me · 01

"Curiosity-driven" decisions

# Curiosity-driven From the first year into college, I constantly generating "how" questions; "how a model predict", "how camera classify objects", "how GPT works" . The visibility of these questions inside my head that got me into anxiety so I decided to solve this questions iteratively. After 2 years into the "scientist role", most of questions about AI (or Models, that's what I usually call them) have answers (certified by Masters, PhDs, and by me coding, reflecting original papers)
  • "And yes, I've re-implemented the base architecture of GPT model for 7 hours"
  • "I have won a debate against a PhD utilizing this knowledge (how did i know that I won? Cause he admitted that my statement is correct and I get kicked out the lab afterward :Đ)"
So if you are learning about Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or AI core concepts, you can take a look at my notes. Feel free to contact to ask question about the notes or any abstract ideas that you're not clear." Recently, my question has shifted into "how can I solve this problem?". I'm currently seeking problems from my perspective to make useful projects, websites. I encourage you to take a look at the projects; some can be interacted with, but some is still in theory. In search of knowledge, I hope that these ideas spark you motivations, especially questions. Sincerely Dat Nguyen
